results.content:
**Definition 3.1.** For a standard classification task with $K$ classes, Label Smoothing (LS) converts a one-hot label $\mathbf{y} \in \mathbb{R}^K$ into a softened target label $\mathbf{s} \in \mathbb{R}^K$:
$$s_k = (1 - \alpha) y_k + \frac{\alpha}{K},$$
(1)
where $y_k = \mathbb{1}_{\{k = gt\}}$ denotes the ground-truth class. The smoothing factor $\alpha \in [0, 1]$ reduces the confidence assigned to the ground-truth class and distributes $\frac{\alpha}{K}$ to other classes uniformly.
results.route_rationale: Definitional formula; the checkable property is that s is a valid probability distribution (Σ_k s_k = 1, each s_k ∈ [0,1]). Trivial algebra, no formalisation needed.

fallback_result.reasoning: Definition 3.1 asserts s_k = (1−α)y_k + α/K. Checkable properties: (i) Σ_k s_k = (1−α)Σ_k y_k + Σ_k α/K = (1−α)·1 + α = 1 since y is one-hot and K terms each contribute α/K; (ii) each s_k ∈ [0,1]: for k=gt, s_gt = (1−α) + α/K ∈ [0,1]; for k≠gt, s_k = α/K ∈ [0,1]. So s is a valid probability distribution, consistent with the LS construction. No error.

results.location: 3.1 Revisiting Label Smoothing / Appendix A (Proof of Lemma 3.2)
results.content:
**Lemma 3.2.** Decomposition of Cross-Entropy Loss with Soft Labels.
$$H(\mathbf{s}, \mathbf{q}) = H(\mathbf{y}, \mathbf{q}) + L_{LS},$$
(2)
where
$$L_{LS} = \alpha \left( H\left(\frac{1}{K}, \mathbf{q}\right) - H(\mathbf{y}, \mathbf{q}) \right).$$
(3)

Where q is the predicted probability vector, H(·) denotes the Cross-Entropy, and 1/K is the uniform distribution introduced by LS. (Appendix A proof: H(s,q) = −Σ_k [(1−α)y_k + α/K] log q_k = (1−α)H(y,q) + αH(1/K,q) = H(y,q) + α(H(1/K,q) − H(y,q)).)
results.route_rationale: Foundational cross-entropy decomposition; formalisable and load-bearing for the rest of the paper.

lean_result.reasoning: Formalised Lemma 3.2 as `ls_decomposition`: with H(p,q) = −Σ_k p_k log q_k and s_k = (1−α)y_k + α/K, H(s,q) = H(y,q) + α(H(u,q) − H(y,q)) where u is the uniform distribution u_k = 1/K. Lean 4 accepted the proof; the identity is purely algebraic in the label mixture and needs no probability/one-hot constraints. Compiler exit 0, no diagnostics, only standard Mathlib axioms (no sorryAx).

lean.formal_statement: theorem ls_decomposition {K : Type*} [Fintype K] (α : ℝ) (y q : K → ℝ) : crossEntropy (fun k => (1 - α) * y k + α / (Fintype.card K : ℝ)) q = crossEntropy y q + α * (crossEntropy (fun _ => (1 / (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℝ)) q - crossEntropy y q) := by simp_rw [add_mul, mul_assoc]; rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib]; rw [← Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.mul_sum]; ring_nf

results.content:
Theorem 3.3. Logit-Level Formulation of Label Smoothing Loss.

While a direct closed-form expression is complex due to the softmax normalization, the effective Label Smoothing loss can be approximated by:

LLS ≈ α ( zgt − (1/K) ∑_{k=1}^K zk ) − log \sum_{j=1}^K e^{z_j}

Here, zgt is the logit of the ground-truth class, and the log-sum-exp term accounts for normalization.
results.route_rationale: Displayed identity; candidate inconsistency with Appendix B eq. (18). Refutable via the log-sum-exp cancellation.

lean_result.reasoning: Formalised the display as an exact equality (`paper_thm33_display`): L_LS = α(z_gt − (1/K)Σz) − log(Σ e^z), where L_LS = α(H(1/K,q) − H(y,q)) from Lemma 3.2 with q = softmax(z), y one-hot at gt. Lean 4 proved the negation (`paper_thm33_display_false`): the display forces log(Σ_j e^{z_j}) = 0 for all z, contradicted at K=2, z = (0,0), gt=0, α=1 (left side L_LS = 0, display right side = −log 2 ≠ 0). In the same file Lean also proved `lls_logit_identity`: L_LS = α(z_gt − (1/K)Σz) exactly — the normalization constant cancels. So the printed display (with the extra −log Σ e^z term) is mathematically wrong; Appendix B eq. (18) and every downstream use (Table 1, Table 11, the eq. (8) comparison) carry the correct formula.
contradiction_locations: 3.1 Revisiting Label Smoothing (Theorem 3.3 display) vs Appendix B (eq. 18)

results.content:
Corollary 3.4. Decomposition of Label Smoothing Loss.

LLS = (α/K) ∑_{zm<zgt} (zgt − zm) + (α/K) ∑_{zn>zgt} (zgt − zn),
(5)

Regularization / Error amplification

where M and N are the numbers of logits below and above zgt, respectively (M + N = K − 1). Note that the error amplification term vanishes when zgt = zmax.
results.route_rationale: Straightforward finite-sum split of L_LS = α/K Σ_k (z_gt − z_k) by ordering relative to z_gt; checkable by inspection. The M+N = K−1 statement assumes no ties (minor technical caveat, not an error).

fallback_result.reasoning: From Appendix B eq. (18), L_LS = α(z_gt − (1/K)Σ_k z_k) = (α/K)Σ_k (z_gt − z_k). Splitting the K summands: the k=gt term contributes 0; logits below z_gt give positive terms (α/K)(z_gt − z_m); logits above give negative terms (α/K)(z_gt − z_n). So eq. (5) is an exact identity. The error-amplification term (second sum) is negative for z_n > z_gt; minimising it drives z_gt down and z_n up (widening the gap), consistent with the paper's reading. Caveat: M + N = K − 1 assumes no logit equals z_gt other than z_gt itself; with ties M + N < K − 1 but the identity still holds because the omitted equal terms are zero. Not an error.

results.content:
Definition 3.5. Max Suppression Regularization

We define the Cross-Entropy loss with MaxSup as follows:

$$\underbrace{H(\mathbf{s}, \mathbf{q})}_{\text{CE with Soft Labels}} = \underbrace{H(\mathbf{y}, \mathbf{q})}_{\text{CE with Hard Labels}} + \underbrace{L_{\text{MaxSup}}}_{\text{Max Suppression Loss}} , \tag{6}$$

where

$$L_{\text{MaxSup}} = \alpha \left( H\!\left(\frac{1}{K}, \mathbf{q}\right) - H(\mathbf{y}', \mathbf{q})\right), \tag{7}$$

and

$$y'_k = \mathbb{1}_{\{k=\arg\max(\mathbf{q})\}},$$

so that $y'_k = 1$ identifies the model's top-1 prediction and $y'_k = 0$ otherwise.
results.route_rationale: Definition of the MaxSup loss; the derived logit-level identity (eq. 8) is machine-checked separately as paper::EQUATION::1.

fallback_result.reasoning: Definition 3.5 defines L_MaxSup = α(H(1/K,q) − H(y',q)) with y' one-hot at argmax(q). y' is a valid one-hot vector, so H(y',q) is a well-defined cross-entropy. The identity eq. (6), H(s,q) = H(y,q) + L_MaxSup, holds by construction of L_MaxSup (the right-hand side is the definition of the 'CE with soft labels'). Consistency with the logit-level form eq. (8) is verified separately by Lean (paper::EQUATION::1). No error.

results.content:
Logit-Level Formulation of MaxSup

Building on the logit-level perspective introduced for LS in Section 3.1, we can express $L_{\text{MaxSup}}$ as:

$$L_{\text{MaxSup}} = \alpha \left( z_{max} - \frac{1}{K} \sum_{k=1}^{K} z_k \right), \tag{8}$$

where $z_{max} = \max_k\{z_k\}$ is the largest (top-1) logit, and $\frac{1}{K} \sum_{k=1}^{K} z_k$ is the mean logit.
results.route_rationale: Closed-form identity following from eq. (7) via exact log-sum-exp cancellation; formalisable.

lean_result.reasoning: Formalised eq. (8) as `eq8_maxsup`: with m a maximum index of z (z_m = z_max, i.e. ∀ k, z_k ≤ z_m), L_MaxSup = α(H(1/K,q) − H(y',q)) with y' one-hot at m equals α(z_m − (1/K)Σz). The supporting lemma `lmaxsup_logit_identity` proves the identity for any index m (no maximality needed); the softmax normalisation constant cancels exactly. Lean 4 accepted the proof; exit 0, no diagnostics, only standard Mathlib axioms.

lean.formal_statement: theorem eq8_maxsup {K : Type*} [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] [Nonempty K] (α : ℝ) (z : K → ℝ) (m : K) (hm : ∀ k, z k ≤ z m) : LMaxSup α z m = α * (z m - (1 / (Fintype.card K : ℝ)) * ∑ k, z k) := by exact lmaxsup_logit_identity α z m

results.content:
Gradient Analysis.
Taking the gradient of the MaxSup loss in Equation (8), which involves both the max logit and the mean of all logits, yields:
$$
\frac{\partial L_{\text{MaxSup}}}{\partial z_k} = \alpha \left( \mathbf{1}_{k = \arg\max(\mathbf{q})} - \frac{1}{K} \right).
$$

Therefore, the top-1 logit receives a positive gradient scaled by α(1 - 1/K), pushing it down, while all other logits receive a negative gradient of magnitude α/K, pushing them slightly up.
results.route_rationale: Subgradient/coefficient claim of the linear map z ↦ α(z_max − mean z); formalisable as the coefficient vector of that linear form.

lean_result.reasoning: Formalised the gradient claim as `gradient_formula`: for L(z) = α(z_m − (1/K)Σz) (the logit-level MaxSup loss, m the max index), the coefficient vector v_k = α(1_{k=m} − 1/K) reconstructs L, i.e. Σ_k v_k z_k = L(z), so ∂L/∂z_k = v_k. Also proved `gradCoeff_top` (v_m = α(1 − 1/K), positive) and `gradCoeff_other` (v_k = −α/K for k ≠ m, negative of magnitude α/K), matching the prose. Lean 4 accepted all proofs; exit 0, no diagnostics, only standard Mathlib axioms.

results.content:
Proof. We aim to prove the equation:
L_{LS} = \alpha ( z_{gt} - \frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K} z_k ) (18)

... The proof derives:
H(\mathbf{s}, \mathbf{q}) = -(1-\alpha)z_{gt} - \frac{\alpha}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K} z_k + \log\Big(\sum_{j=1}^{K} e^{z_j}\Big) (24)
H(\mathbf{y}, \mathbf{q}) = -z_{gt} + \log\Big(\sum_{j=1}^{K} e^{z_j}\Big).
Therefore,
H(\mathbf{s}, \mathbf{q}) - H(\mathbf{y}, \mathbf{q}) = \alpha z_{gt} - \frac{\alpha}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K} z_k,
which proves (18).
results.route_rationale: The exact logit-level LS identity that Theorem 3.3's proof establishes; the load-bearing equation for the paper's LS analysis.

lean_result.reasoning: Formalised Appendix B eq. (18) as `appendix_eq18`: with L_LS = α(H(1/K,q) − H(y,q)) from Lemma 3.2, q = softmax(z), y one-hot at gt, L_LS = α(z_gt − (1/K)Σz). The proof implements the paper's own derivation: the log-sum-exp terms cancel exactly, leaving no normalization constant. Lean 4 accepted the proof; exit 0, no diagnostics, only standard Mathlib axioms. (This is the correct version of Theorem 3.3, contrasting with the erroneous main-body display refuted in paper::EQUATION::0.)

results.location: Appendix B (Proof of Theorem 3.3, CutMix/Mixup case)
results.content:
Due to the broad usage of CutMix and Mixup in the training recipe of modern Neural Networks, we additionally take their impact into account together with Label Smoothing. Now we additionally prove the case with CutMix and Mixup:

$$L'_{LS} = \alpha\Big((\lambda z_{gt1} + (1-\lambda)z_{gt2}) - \frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K} z_k\Big)$$
(27)

With CutMix and Mixup, the smoothed label becomes:

$$s_k = (1-\alpha)(\lambda y_{k1} + (1-\lambda)y_{k2}) + \frac{\alpha}{K}$$
(28)

where $y_{k1}$ and $y_{k2}$ are one-hot vectors for the two ground truth classes from mixing, and $\lambda$ is the mixing ratio.
results.route_rationale: Direct generalisation of the machine-checked eq. (18) by linearity of the mixing; informal review suffices once eq. (18) is verified.

fallback_result.reasoning: With the mixed label y' = λy_1 + (1−λ)y_2, H(y',q) = −(λ log q_gt1 + (1−λ) log q_gt2) = −(λz_gt1 + (1−λ)z_gt2) + log Z (Z = Σ e^{z_j}), using the one-hot sums and log q_k = z_k − log Z. H(1/K,q) = −(1/K)Σz_k + log Z. Then L'_LS = α(H(1/K,q) − H(y',q)) = α[(λz_gt1 + (1−λ)z_gt2) − (1/K)Σz_k], exactly eq. (27). The derivation in eqs. (29)–(40) matches this. No error.

results.content:
C.1 New Objective Function

The Cross Entropy with Max Suppression is defined as:

$$L_{\text{MaxSup},t}(x, y) = H\left(y_k + \frac{\alpha}{K} - \alpha \cdot \mathbf{1}_{k=\text{argmax}(\mathbf{q})},\, q_t^S(x)\right)$$

C.2 Gradient Analysis

The gradient of the loss with respect to the logit $$z_i$$ for each class $$i$$ is derived as:

$$\partial_i^{\text{MaxSup},t} = q_{t,i} - y_i - \frac{\alpha}{K} + \alpha \cdot \mathbf{1}_{i=\text{argmax}(\mathbf{q})}$$
results.route_rationale: Standard cross-entropy gradient identity ∂H(p,softmax(z))/∂z_i = q_i − p_i applied to the MaxSup pseudo-target; informal check conclusive, heavier to fully formalise.

fallback_result.reasoning: Let p_i = y_i + α/K − α·1_{i=argmax(q)}. Then L_MaxSup,t = H(p, q). For q = softmax(z), ∂H(p,q)/∂z_i = q_i − p_i (standard: ∂/∂z_i[−Σ_j p_j log q_j] = −p_i + q_i·Σ_j p_j = q_i − p_i, using Σ_j p_j = 1). Hence ∂_i = q_{t,i} − y_i − α/K + α·1_{i=argmax(q)}, exactly as printed. The pseudo-target p sums to 1 (Σ_k y_k + α − α = 1). Presentational caveat, not a mathematical error: in a misclassification p_gt = 1 + α/K > 1 and p_{argmax} = −α(1 − 1/K) < 0, so p is not a bona fide probability vector, but cross-entropy remains well-defined for such a signed pseudo-target and the gradient identity is unaffected.

results.content:
Scenario 1: Model makes correct prediction. When the model correctly predicts the target class (argmax(q) = GT), the gradients are:
• For the target class (GT): ∂_{\mathrm{GT}}^{\mathrm{MaxSup},t} = q_{t,\mathrm{GT}} - \left(1 - \alpha\!\left(1 - \frac{1}{K}\right)\right)
• For non-target classes: ∂_{i}^{\mathrm{MaxSup},t} = q_{t,i} - \frac{\alpha}{K}

Scenario 2: Model makes wrong prediction. When the model incorrectly predicts the most confident class (argmax(q) ≠ GT), the gradients are:
• For the target class (GT): ∂_{\mathrm{GT}}^{\mathrm{MaxSup},t} = q_{t,\mathrm{GT}} - \left(1 + \frac{\alpha}{K}\right)
• For non-target classes (not most confident): ∂_{i}^{\mathrm{MaxSup},t} = q_{t,i} - \frac{\alpha}{K}
• For the most confident non-target class: ∂_{i}^{\mathrm{MaxSup},t} = q_{t,i} + \alpha\!\left(1 - \frac{1}{K}\right)
results.route_rationale: Direct substitution of y_i and the argmax indicator into the verified C.2 formula; checks internal consistency of the two scenarios.

fallback_result.reasoning: Substituting into ∂_i = q_{t,i} − y_i − α/K + α·1_{i=argmax(q)}: Scenario 1 (GT = argmax): GT → y=1, 1_{GT=argmax}=1, so ∂_GT = q_GT − 1 − α/K + α = q_GT − (1 − α(1−1/K)) ✓; non-target → y=0, indicator=0, ∂_i = q_i − α/K ✓. Scenario 2 (GT ≠ argmax): GT → y=1, indicator=0, ∂_GT = q_GT − 1 − α/K = q_GT − (1 + α/K) ✓; most confident non-target → y=0, indicator=1, ∂_i = q_i − α/K + α = q_i + α(1−1/K) ✓; other non-targets → q_i − α/K ✓. All four printed formulas match, and the interpretation is consistent: on misclassification the wrong top-1 logit is pushed down and the ground-truth logit up (since gradient descent subtracts a positive gradient from the top-1 and adds to GT). The claim 'Max Suppression is equivalent to Label Smoothing for correct predictions' also holds: for argmax(q)=GT, y'=y so L_MaxSup = α(H(1/K,q)−H(y,q)) = L_LS. No error.

findings.evidence: Lean 4 refuted the main-body Theorem 3.3 display $L_{LS} \approx \alpha(z_{gt} - \frac{1}{K}\sum_k z_k) - \log\sum_j e^{z_j}$. With $L_{LS}$ defined as in Lemma 3.2 and $q = \operatorname{softmax}(z)$, the softmax normalisation constant cancels exactly, giving (and Lean proves) the identity $L_{LS} = \alpha(z_{gt} - \frac{1}{K}\sum_k z_k)$ — the printed display forces $\log\sum_j e^{z_j} = 0$ for all $z$, refuted at $z = (0,0)$, $K=2$ (left side $0$, right side $-\log 2$). Appendix B eq. (18) and every downstream use (Table 1, Table 11, the eq. (8) comparison) carry the correct formula, so the paper's argument survives; the error is a mis-statement of the theorem's displayed formula in the main body.
findings.exact_quote: LLS ≈ α ( zgt − (1/K) ∑_{k=1}^K zk ) − log \sum_{j=1}^K e^{z_j}

summary:
Verified the mathematics of 'MaxSup: Overcoming Representation Collapse in Label Smoothing' (paper.md). 11 self-contained mathematical objects were extracted and routed: 5 to Lean 4 (verify-math-lean, one shared project MATH_VERIFICATION/Paper, run strictly serially) and 6 to informal review (verify-math).

Lean settled all 5 formal claims: Lemma 3.2 (cross-entropy decomposition), eq. (8) (MaxSup logit-level identity), the Section 3.2 gradient formula, and Appendix B eq. (18) (LS logit-level identity) all PASSED; the main-body Theorem 3.3 display was REFUTED — Lean proved the negation, establishing that the printed formula carries a spurious $-\log\sum_j e^{z_j}$ term. This is reported as one minor finding (paper::EQUATION::0): the main-body display contradicts the appendix proof (eq. 18) that the paper itself carries, and the correct formula is used everywhere downstream, so the argument survives.

The 6 informal reviews (Definitions 3.1 & 3.5, Corollary 3.4, Appendix B eq. 27 CutMix/Mixup, Appendix C gradient formula, Appendix C Scenarios 1-2) all came back clean; the only caveats noted are non-errors: the M+N=K−1 statement in Corollary 3.4 assumes no tied logits (the identity still holds), and the Appendix C.1 pseudo-target can leave [0,1] in misclassifications (cross-entropy is still well-defined).

No Lean result was FAILED or NOT_ATTEMPTED, so no informal fallbacks were required. The shared Lean project MATH_VERIFICATION/Paper pre-existed this run (it contains verified proofs from other papers), so per the verify-math-lean deletion rules it was reused, not created, and was therefore kept on disk (lean_project_kept: true); its Mathlib build was reused for all five serial verifications.

Verdict: MINOR_ERRORS — one confident, formally-refuted mis-statement of a theorem formula; no error invalidates any main claim.
